title: Percentile-Curve Inference for Flat Conditional Treatment Effects from Confounded Observational Records
banked_reason: The core offers neither a matched converse, a stated strict improvement over a published bound, nor a first result for a distinct causal estimand: q_P=c is the common ATE and the random percentile target is self-stipulated, so this bespoke-estimator analysis is presently letter-tier, below novelty_target=field.

proof_attempt_summary: Literature review and a corrected proto-core explored uniform same-data percentile reconstruction under rough confounding. The reviewer and independent D/main consults found the causal percentile target is only the common ATE, while the nonconstant target is a stipulated random oracle; no faithful field-tier reframe exists within the fixed contract. No D0 derivation or Lean proof was attempted, and oracle reconstruction, Gaussian process convergence, feasible centering and certified bands remain unproved.
tldr: An estimated effect distribution can display spread when its true causal percentile curve is constant. Dette--Kroll--Volgushev (2026) establishes flat rearrangement limits for uniform-density histograms and independent-copula estimators. The open statistical question here is whether original observational records with unknown H\"older-one-third confounding can reproduce the entire realized percentile curve of the stipulated causal box oracle at an error smaller than \(n^{-1/2}\). The binary-outcome benchmark maintains bespoke interior arm-mean ranges and a compact common-effect range. An occupancy-weighted fine-cell handle preserves the original counts; a boundary-aware estimated normal-mixture center removes the larger noise spread. The proposal couples that reconstruction question to a uniform marked-record percentile law and finite simulated simultaneous bands of root-n width on \(U\).
gap: The verified histogram and independent-copula results of Dette--Kroll--Volgushev (2026), and stationary occupation theory, do not state this original-record causal reconstruction and feasible calibration bundle. The two adjacent 2026 effect-distribution manuscripts remain unresolved containment risks.
fill: Conditional count expansions and exact population sorting address reconstruction; finite-window variance-mixture centering and certified Gaussian calibration address simultaneous inference. The central construction is an open-ended question rather than an assumed nuisance-rate statement.
